newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACCC recommends lower Telstra interconnect fees.
newsitem.headline: ACCC recommends lower Telstra interconnect fees.

text.p: Anti-monoplies authority, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), said on Wednesday that it recommended lower interconnect fees with Telstra Corp main network from July 1, 1997.

ACCC, which will become regulator of the local telecoms market when its deregulated next month, said the main usage charges for interconnection had been reduced by over 40 percent to 2.74 cents per minute from 4.41 cents per minute in peak periods.
In off-peak periods, the fees would drop to 1.19 cents from 2.35 cents, the ACCC said.

The ACCC said the draft determination reduces the charges for Telstra's National Access service, which is currently used by a number of switched service providers to connect to and provide services, using the Telstra network.
The government owned Telstra monopoly on the local telecom market has been partly broken following partial deregulation in 1992. The era of full deregulation starts on July 1.
However, the prices will apply until December 31, 1997. From January 1, 1998 these charges will be subject to commercial negotiation between Telstra and industry players, the ACCC said.
The ACCC said it will arbitrate disputes if charges cannot be agreed upon at the time.
The ACCC is seeking comments on the draft determination by June 17, 1997 before making a final determination before July 1.
